Plot corpus coverage

entropia_plot_coverage.Rd

Plots the output of entropia_corpus_quality() – coverage proportions per metric and group – as a bar chart. With a single metric the chart is a plain bar chart of the coverage proportion by group; with several metrics the bars are faceted by metric, each panel carrying its own groups and y scale.

Usage

entropia_plot_coverage(x, metric = NULL)

Arguments

x

A data frame or tibble with metric, group and pct columns, e.g. the output of entropia_corpus_quality().

metric

Optional character vector of metric(s) to plot, a subset of unique(x$metric). NULL (default) plots all metrics.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The y axis is labelled as a percentage. pct is NA for groups with no total (e.g. a metric absent from a corpus); these rows receive an explicit annotation, using status when available, instead of a misleading zero bar. Optional group_id is displayed alongside the label; distinct IDs never merge. Empty selections produce a Spanish no-data annotation.

Examples

q <- data.frame(
  metric = c("ocr_coverage", "metadata_coverage"),
  group = c("image", "Archivo de prueba"),
  n = c(250L, 3L),
  total = c(2428L, 3L),
  pct = c(250 / 2428, 1)
)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- entropia_plot_coverage(q)
  p + ggplot2::labs(title = "Cobertura")
}
